# Lighting and Appearance Models

Also called: Appearance Modeling, View-Dependent Rendering Models

## Overview
Lighting and Appearance Models define how a Neural Radiance Field represents and renders the visual appearance of a scene, specifically addressing view-dependent effects such as specular highlights, subsurface scattering, and stylized textures. While standard NeRF maps 3D coordinates and view directions directly to color via a dense MLP, these models decouple geometry from appearance or replace the implicit color prediction with explicit physical or generative priors . They differ from siblings like [Spherical Harmonics NeRF](14480-spherical-harmonics-nerf.md) by using explicit basis functions for relighting, and from [Neural Pre-Integrated Lighting (Neural-PIL)](13783-neural-pre-integrated-lighting-neural-pil.md) by avoiding pre-integrated light queries in favor of direct coefficient optimization.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family replace or augment the standard NeRF color prediction head $f_\Theta(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \to (\sigma, \mathbf{c})$ with a specialized appearance module. The core principle is the separation of volumetric density $\sigma$ (geometry) from radiance or color $\mathbf{c}$ (appearance), allowing the appearance component to be conditioned on external factors such as lighting embeddings, style vectors, or explicit illumination bases. The rendering equation remains the standard volume rendering integral, but the emitted radiance term is computed via the specific model's output rather than a direct MLP regression .

## Subtopics

### [Neural Pre-Integrated Lighting (Neural-PIL)](13783-neural-pre-integrated-lighting-neural-pil.md)
Neural-PIL replaces numerical light integration with a neural network that predicts pre-integrated light $\tilde{L}_i$ directly from an illumination embedding, direction, and roughness. It uses a pi-GAN-based MLP with FiLM-SIREN layers to capture fine illumination details that Spherical Harmonics miss. Choose this when high-fidelity specular reflections and relighting are required without the memory cost of high-order SH bases.

### [Spherical Harmonics NeRF](14480-spherical-harmonics-nerf.md)
Spherical Harmonics NeRF replaces the view-dependent color MLP with an explicit 2nd-order SH illumination model. It computes a normal from density gradients and evaluates SH basis functions to modulate accumulated albedo. Choose this when explicit relighting and semantic lighting control are needed, as it allows varying learnable SH coefficients per image.

### [StylizedNeRF](14882-stylizednerf.md)
StylizedNeRF integrates style-based generation (inspired by StyleGAN2) into the NeRF backbone. It uses a mapping network to generate style vectors from latent codes, which modulate features via affine transformations and convolutions. Choose this for high-resolution, 3D-consistent style transfer, decoupling geometry from 2D appearance styles.

## Background
The standard NeRF formulation [Parent](3065-nerf-hyperparameters.md) assumes a fixed lighting environment and predicts color implicitly. As NeRF applications expanded to dynamic lighting and artistic styles, explicit appearance models became necessary. Neural-PIL and Spherical Harmonics NeRF emerged to address the limitations of implicit color prediction in handling complex lighting . StylizedNeRF adapted generative adversarial networks to NeRFs to enable style transfer .
